name: Cordel xilogravura
summary: A woodcut for the cover of a cordel chapbook, a cheap booklet of verse that hangs from a string. The cutter works in a soft wood, with bold white lines, flat shapes and one black ink.

philosophy.core_thesis: One woodcut on a cheap cover can tell the whole story of a verse in a single bold picture.
design_principles: Cut the block in a soft wood with a knife and a gouge.
Make a strong, simple scene: a hero, an animal, a saint or a bandit, drawn full-face or in profile.
Use a thick black mass with white outline and a repeat pattern in the background.
Cut the title into the block, in simple blocky letters, or set it in type.
Print in black on a coloured paper cover; the paper gives the second colour.
Keep the picture to a small size, about A6 to A5.
Leave the wood grain and the knife marks in view.
anti_patterns: Many colours with an even blend

process.matrix: A soft wood block, such as umburana or imbuia, cut with a knife and a gouge.
process.press: Hand rubbing with a spoon, or a small letterpress.
process.image_making: The cutter draws the scene on the block, then cuts away the white areas.
process.edition: Hundreds to thousands of covers from one block.

inks.strategy: One black ink on a coloured paper cover; the paper stands for the second ink.

colours.name: Cover paper red
colours.role: the coloured cover stock, a stand-in for a second ink

screening.rule: Make a tone with the width and the spacing of knife lines and with repeat marks, 0.4–1.5 mm apart; do not use a screen.

registration.rule: One block prints the picture; a second block, if used, can sit 1 mm off.

substrate.stock: A cheap newsprint for the pages and a thicker coloured paper for the cover.
substrate.finish: Uncoated and matt, with a rough tooth.

surface.impression: A light bite with a clear edge on the black areas.
surface.texture: Solid black with a mottled grain, white knife lines and repeat patterns.

positive: bold black and white gouge lines

evidence.title: Xilogravura Lucélia Borges
evidence.credit: Lucélia Borges, Wikimedia Commons (a modern work)

emotion.target_response: Storytelling warmth: the viewer feels a lively voice from a market square.

avoid_when: The subject needs tonal depth or a likeness.
The tone must be luxury or technical.

modifiers.how: Use larger black masses, a hand-lettered slogan and a heroic group figure.
Cut thin, parallel shading lines and print on laid paper.
